newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Suit, job claims inflame Conrail battle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Suit, job claims inflame Conrail battle.

text.p: A bitter takeover battle for Conrail Inc. intensified Thursday in an exchange of legal action and accusations ahead of a key shareholder vote.

Conrail and CSX Corp., which have proposed an $8.7 billion merger, said they had sued rival bidder Norfolk Southern Corp. in U.S. District Court, accusing it of trying to break up their deal with no intention of acquiring the railroad for itself.
The suit seeks a jury trial and punitive damages, but does not specify an amount, according to a copy of the complaint.
Meanwhile, Norfolk Southern extended its campaign for the support of Conrail employees and Pennsylvania political leaders in its $10 billion bid for the Philadelphia-based Conrail.
Norfolk Southern said it was more likely to provide secure jobs and pensions, as well as other economic benefits to the state.

Norfolk Southern told the Pennsylvania state retirement system, a Conrail shareholder, that a CSX-Conrail deal would cause "major job losses," particularly in Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware and Ohio, due to duplications in the two railroads' systems.

"As the Conrail and Norfolk Southern rail systems complement each other, job losses will be less in the Norfolk Southern proposal," Norfolk Southern said in a response to questions from the state retirement system.
The responses were contained in documents filed with federal regulators Thursday.
Norfolk Southern has made similar claims in court and in full-page advertisements in major Pennsylvania newspapers Wednesday.
Conrail has said there would be some initial job losses, but the long-term impact of the merger would be to increase growth at the merged railroad.

Conrail employees, through an employee stock ownership plan and separate employee benefits trust, control a key block of stock -- more than 10 percent -- ahead of a Dec. 23 Conrail company meeting at which shareholders will vote on whether to allow the cash-and-stock merger with CSX to proceed.
Representatives of both sides in the battle have said the vote could be very close.
Conrail and CSX said in announcing their suit that Norfolk Southern had no intention of completing its all-cash bid.

"Norfolk Southern is acting not with the intention or expectation of acquiring Conrail shares at $110 per share but in order to disrupt and cripple a strategic alliance between CSX and Conrail," the two railroads said.
"Despite Norfolk Southern's ongoing campaign to destroy the CSX/Conrail strategic merger, we are confident the merger will be successfully completed," they said.
Norfolk Southern spokesman Rob Chapman said, "The Conrail-CSX claim is frivolous, an obvious attempt to divert attention away from the fact that the CSX-Conrail deal remains inferior."

Norfolk Southern has said only the actions of Conrail's board would prevent its bid from succeeding. Conrail's merger agreement with CSX contains several provisions to "lock-up" the deal between the two.

Conrail and CSX said in their suit that Conrail would have to breach its merger agreement with CSX for the Norfolk Southern offer to succeed, or that CSX's consent would be needed if the merger agreement were to be terminated.

Norfolk Southern earlier sued in federal court to block the Conrail-CSX merger, but failed in its request for an emergency injunction to block the first step in the deal -- a cash tender offer by CSX for 19.9 percent of Conrail shares.
CSX stock gained $1 to $47.75 on the New York Stock Exchange, Conrail rose 25 cents to $96.75, while Norfolk Southern rose 25 cents to $88.625.
